cover.headline: A good fluoropolymer business carrying an unproven ₹6,000 cr battery bet, priced as if the bet has paid off
cover.lead: Gujarat Fluorochemicals (GFL) is India's largest maker of fluoropolymers (PTFE, PVDF, FKM, PFA: 63% of FY26 revenue), a large refrigerant producer (21%, now booming on its new R32 plant) and a bulk-chemicals maker (13%). It is also building a battery-materials business, GFCL EV, which has absorbed ~₹2,000 cr so far and will take ₹6,000 cr by FY28, yet sold only ₹14 cr in Q1FY27. Most brokers value GFL on **P/E on FY28E earnings** (Prabhudas Lilladher 52x; ICICI Direct's 30x EV/EBITDA is ~54x P/E). We use the same method: **32x Sep-28E EPS of ₹98.1** gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**, so **we initiate with SELL.** The EV/EBITDA cross-check (₹3,699) is higher because its starting multiple still includes the trough years; the DCF (₹1,513) shows that cash flows support far less while capex and working capital absorb all the cash. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Q1FY27 revenue rose 24% and net profit 20%. Fluoropolymers grew 15% on higher-value grades, refrigerants 52% on R32 (10kt plant full, doubling to 20kt in Q2FY27), and the Chemicals segment's EBITDA margin reached 29%. 3M has left the market and AGC plans to shut its UK plant. Management guides 15-20% a year for fluoropolymers.

arguments.h: The battery business is still a promise
arguments.p: GFCL EV had ₹33 cr of segment revenue and an ₹80 cr EBITDA loss in FY26; Q1FY27 revenue was ₹14 cr with a ₹30 cr loss. The Oman plant is on hold and its ~₹1,200 cr of sovereign funding is lost. Management now targets ₹100 cr+ of quarterly revenue by Q4FY27 and the full potential only by FY29.

arguments.h: Returns are below the cost of capital, and debt is rising
arguments.p: Return on equity was ~8% in each of FY24-26. Capex of ₹3,150 cr in FY27 and ~₹2,400 cr in FY28, plus heavy working capital (inventory ~450 days), take net debt from ₹2,094 cr to ~₹7,029 cr by FY28 on our numbers. We forecast ROE of only 11.6% in FY29.

At ₹4,405 the stock trades at 49.6x our FY28E EPS. Chemical peers have de-rated ~28% against their five-year P/E medians; GFL has re-rated (trailing P/E 79.0x vs a 55.5x median). After valuing chemicals at 20x EBITDA, the price implies ~₹10,063 cr for a battery business that still loses money.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first quarter with the 20kt R32 plant, and whether battery revenue starts to climb.
New funding for GFCL EV to replace the Oman sovereign money: how much, at what valuation, and how much of the subsidiary GFL keeps.
Battery revenue against management's target of ₹100 cr+ in Q4FY27; LFP cathode and PVDF binder qualifications.
EU PFAS restriction: ECHA's socio-economic committee (SEAC) final opinion expected by end-2026; fluoropolymers are in scope.
India: HFC quota rules (baseline set from Jan-2027), the PTFE anti-dumping case filed by GFL (Mar-2026) and the R-125 duty recommended in Sep-2026.
Approvals for the scheme merging promoter company Inox Leasing and Finance into GFL.

sections.title: One fluorine chain, four businesses

blocks.p: GFL is the chemicals arm of the INOX group (the Jain family), which also controls Inox Wind and Inox Clean Energy. Its businesses form one chain. Fluorspar (it owns a mine in Morocco) becomes hydrofluoric acid (HF); HF plus chloroform from its own chlor-alkali plant makes the refrigerant R22; R22 is cracked into TFE, the building block of PTFE and other fluoropolymers. Each step adds value and gives GFL control over cost and quality that importers do not have. It runs three sites in Gujarat (Ranjitnagar, Dahej and Jolva) and warehouses in Europe, the US and the Middle East. Exports are about 60% of revenue; no customer is more than 10%.

blocks.callout: **Corporate actions since listing (2019):** no bonus, split, buyback or equity issue at GFL; share count unchanged at 10.985 cr. Dividends are small (₹3 a share for FY26). Every new round at GFCL EV reduces GFL shareholders' share of the battery business.

sections.title: Fluoropolymers: a ~US$10 bn market with few makers; refrigerants: rationed by regulation

blocks.p: Fluoropolymers are plastics and rubbers built on carbon-fluorine bonds, the strongest in organic chemistry. They resist heat, chemicals, fire and weather, and nothing else does all of that, so they are used in chemical plants, cables, car engines, semiconductor fabs, lithium batteries (PVDF binder) and hydrogen equipment. The global market was ~US$10.3 bn in 2025 and is expected to grow ~6.5% a year to 2030 (MarketsandMarkets, Mar-2026). Supply is concentrated: Chemours, Daikin, Syensqo (ex-Solvay), AGC, Dongyue and a few other Chinese makers, plus GFL. Making them takes hazardous chemistry and years of customer qualification, which keeps the number of suppliers small.

sections.title: Fluoropolymers: steady growth from better grades, with new capacity needed

pair.title: Fluoropolymer revenue: +15% in Q1FY27
Annual: FY23 peak regained in FY26

bullets: **What drives it.** Volume of new fluoropolymers (PFA, FKM, PVDF, FEP), which are "almost fully utilised", and a shift to higher grades in existing products. Management calls price increases "marginal" and mostly formula-based pass-through of input costs (sulphur, fluorspar, methanol rose sharply from Mar-2026).

**Guidance.** 15-20% a year (17-20% in the closing remarks), "absolutely visible" for FY27 and FY28. Most customer approvals are due by end-FY27, and ₹250 cr of new capacity is being added; until then growth comes from debottlenecking and mix.

**Competition.** Management says high-value grades see little direct Chinese competition. In commodity PTFE, China sets the price: Dongyue's 2025 fluoropolymer margin was 9%, and GFL itself has asked India for anti-dumping duties on Chinese PTFE.
**Disclosure gap.** GFL does not disclose fluoropolymer capacity, volumes, prices or margins; we cannot separate volume from price.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is GFL's best business: integrated from fluorspar, qualified with demanding customers, gaining share as Western makers retreat. We model 15% / 16% / 15% growth (FY27-29E), the bottom of guidance, because capacity is tight until the new lines run and Europe (26% of revenue) faces the PFAS restriction from around 2028.

sections.title: Refrigerants: an R32 windfall with a regulatory ceiling; bulk chemicals: steady

pair.title: Fluorochemicals revenue by quarter
Bulk chemicals: flat at ~₹160 cr a quarter

bullets: **R22 is shrinking, R32 is booming.** Fluorochemicals fell from ₹1,518 cr in FY23 to ₹1,074 cr in FY26 as R22 quotas were cut under the Montreal Protocol and US tariffs hit R125. R32 changed that: the 10kt plant started in Mar-2026 and ran full in Q1FY27, lifting the business 52% to ₹458 cr. A second 10kt goes live in Q2FY27; 40-50% of R32 is on long-term contracts and export and domestic prices are "very close".

**R134a and the quota race.** GFL is adding R134a (brownfield, by end-FY27) and AHF, aiming to use its full HFC entitlement before India freezes production in 2028 on a 2024-26 baseline. After 31-Dec-2027 no new HFC capacity will be cleared.

**The ceiling.** From 2028 volumes are capped and fall 10% by 2032; Navin Fluorine (+15kt R32) and SRF are also adding capacity before the cut-off, and calendar 2027 is a "free year" in which new capacity can sell. R32 prices are near multi-year highs.

**Bulk chemicals** (caustic soda, chloromethanes, 13% of revenue) mainly supply GFL's own chain; Q1FY27 revenue rose 11% on price; management expects caustic soda stable and chloromethanes range-bound.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** R32 is a genuine windfall and the main reason FY27 earnings jump. We model fluorochemicals +70% in FY27 (about the Q1 run-rate), +18% in FY28 and +4% in FY29, when quotas bind and new Indian capacity competes. We do not assume today's R32 price lasts beyond FY28.

sections.title: Battery materials: ₹2,000 cr spent, ₹4,000 cr to go, ₹14 cr of sales a quarter

blocks.p: GFCL EV makes the chemicals inside a lithium-ion cell: LiPF6 salt and formulated electrolyte, LFP cathode material, PVDF binder, and soon natural-graphite anode, at an integrated complex at Jolva, Gujarat. The idea is sound: GFL already makes HF, PVDF and fluorine chemicals, and customers outside China want second suppliers. Management targets ₹6,000 cr of cumulative capex by FY28, ~2x asset turns (so ~₹12,000 cr of revenue at full use) and an EBITDA margin above 25%, with full potential by FY29. So far ~₹2,000 cr has been invested.

blocks.title: Moat scorecard
blocks.source: GAM research compilation (filings and calls to Sep-2026)

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** GFL has a **narrow moat in fluoropolymers** (integration, qualifications, scale outside China) and a **time-limited regulatory moat in refrigerants**. It has **no moat yet in battery materials**, which is where most of its capital is going. Because commodity PTFE is priced off China, returns swing with the cycle (ROE 27% in FY23, ~8% in FY24-26) instead of compounding.

sections.title: A boom in FY23, a bust in FY24, and a slow climb back

blocks.p: GFL's results swing with fluoropolymer and refrigerant prices. Revenue rose 44% to ₹5,685 cr in FY23, when PTFE and refrigerant prices were high and the EBITDA margin reached 35%; net profit was a record ₹1,323 cr. In FY24 Chinese supply and customer destocking cut revenue by 25% and net profit by 67% (₹435 cr). Since then the recovery has been slow: FY26 revenue was ₹4,996 cr, still 12% below FY23, and net profit ₹574 cr, 57% below. Q1FY27 was the best quarter since FY23: revenue ₹1,588 cr (+24%) and net profit ₹219 cr (+20%), helped by the new R32 refrigerant plant. (Figures before FY22 are distorted by the 2019 demerger and one-off tax items, so we start the story in FY22.)

pair.title: Depreciation up 79% in four years as plants were added

blocks.callout: **Our view:** GFL is a capital-heavy business in the middle of its biggest investment cycle. Gross block rose from ₹3,680 cr in FY22 to ₹7,053 cr in FY26 and another ₹1,900 cr sits in plants not yet finished. Depreciation and interest have grown faster than profit, and the battery business has added losses (₹104 cr after tax in FY26). Return on equity has been 8% for three years, well below the cost of equity.

sections.title: Five years of capex funded by operating cash and debt; returns have fallen to 8%

blocks.p: Over FY22-26 GFL generated ₹3,612 cr of operating cash and spent ₹4,510 cr on plants: ₹1.25 for every rupee of operating cash. Dividends were small (₹154 cr in five years). The gap was closed with debt and, in FY26, with ₹430 cr from the International Finance Corporation (IFC) at the battery subsidiary. About ₹2,000 cr of the spending went into battery materials, which earned ₹33 cr of segment revenue and lost ₹80 cr at the EBITDA level in FY26. Screener's return on capital employed (ROCE) fell from 30% in FY23 to 10% in FY24-26.

blocks.callout: **Where it went right and wrong:** in FY26 the Chemicals segment earned ₹1,371 cr of EBITDA on ₹6,313 cr of capital employed: a healthy business. The battery segment had ₹1,599 cr of capital employed (₹2,793 cr of assets) and lost money. The company's own ROCE (14.05%) and ROE (12.17%) for FY26 leave out capital in capacity added over the last two years and plants still being built; on all of its equity GFL earned about 7.6%. The next two years will test whether the battery spending earns its cost of capital.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, flattering company metrics

bullets: **Forex gains inside "EBITDA".** The company's segment EBITDA (₹1,291 cr in FY26) includes ₹88.6 cr of net foreign-exchange gains (₹57.8 cr in FY25) that the annual P&L shows as other income. With the rupee at ~₹96/US$ in Jun-2026, these gains may not repeat. We use Screener's annual basis (₹1,201 cr) and assume no forex gains.
**Return metrics exclude the new money.** Company ROCE (14.05%) and ROE (12.17%) for FY26 leave out capital in capacity added over two years and CWIP. On total equity, ROE was ~7.6%.
**IFC money is a liability at fair value.** The ₹430 cr CCPS in GFCL EV are carried at fair value through profit or loss: if the subsidiary's value rises, GFL books a loss.

**Subsidiary stock options at ₹1.** GFCL EV granted 75 lakh options at ₹1 to key managers in FY26 when it was selling shares at ₹35; the DMD's FY26 ESOP charge was ₹8.21 cr. This is a real cost that will grow if GFCL EV succeeds.

**One-offs.** ₹19.5 cr labour-code charge in FY26; Q4FY25 profit included a ₹29 cr deferred-tax gain. In Q1FY27 some export (CIF) sales booked earlier in the US and German trading arms were reversed in the standalone books (consolidated unaffected).
**Working capital.** Inventory of ~450 days of revenue (Screener basis) ties up ₹1,933 cr; any fall in prices would hit inventory values.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** The audit (Patankar & Associates) is unqualified and segment disclosure reconciles. The amber is for presentation choices that flatter: forex gains in EBITDA, ROCE/ROE that exclude new capital, and subsidiary-level options and instruments that sit outside the headline numbers.

sections.title: Debt is rising with the battery build-out; working capital is heavy

blocks.p: Net debt (borrowings less cash and investments) was ₹2,094 cr at March 2026, about 1.7x Screener EBITDA. Borrowings of ₹2,721 cr include ₹430 cr of IFC's convertible preference shares in GFCL EV, which carry no interest but will become equity in the subsidiary. Working capital is the other big use of money: inventories were ₹1,933 cr (453 days of revenue on Screener's cost basis) because GFL keeps 30-90 days of stock in warehouses in the US and Germany and runs integrated chains from fluorspar to polymer. Management cut working-capital days from 192 to 149 in Q1FY27. With ₹3,150 cr of capex planned for FY27 and ~₹2,400 cr more in FY28, we expect net debt to more than triple by FY28.

Promoter family bought GFCL EV shares/warrants at ₹35 (₹200 cr); key managers got GFCL EV options at ₹1; IFC holds convertibles; outsiders own 26% of the Oman unit.
The growth asset is being shared outside GFL.

Smaller than before, but still exposure to Inox group entities.
Patankar & Associates, unqualified. No capacity, volume or margin data by business; company ROCE/ROE exclude new capital.
Hard to check the investment case from outside.
Founder D.K. Jain died Dec-2025; Vivek Jain is chairman and MD; Dr. Bir Kapoor (DMD/CEO) runs operations; four whole-time plant directors.
₹4,510 cr capex in FY22-26 with ROE at ~8%; battery plan cut back in Oman and moved to India; low payout (~6%).
The battery bet decides the verdict.

blocks.p: We forecast revenue by business line. The company discloses profit only for Chemicals and for battery materials, so the three chemical lines share one Chemicals EBITDA margin (29-29.5%, close to Q1FY27's 29.1%, with no forex gains), and battery materials carries its own margin. Capex follows the plan (₹3,150 cr in FY27, ~₹2,400 cr in FY28), so depreciation and interest rise before the battery plants earn. Every assumption is in the Excel model's Assumptions sheet.

blocks.callout: For FY27 we are 13% below consensus EPS, mainly because we assume battery materials still lose ~₹110 cr at the EBITDA level (Q1 alone lost ₹30 cr) rather than breaking even, and because interest rises with net debt. Our FY27 revenue is close to the street. For FY28 our revenue is above Prabhudas Lilladher's and ICICI Direct's (it includes ~₹1,000 cr of battery sales), but our EPS is in line with PL and below ICICI Direct, JM and Elara because we assume a thin battery margin (5%) and interest of ~₹330 cr on rising debt. Our EPS grows ~30% a year over FY26-28E and ~27% over FY26-29E.

sections.title: The street: mostly positive after Q1, but targets sit close to the price

blocks.p: Five houses published after the Q1FY27 results (13-Aug-2026): ICICI Direct BUY ₹5,800, ICICI Securities ₹5,050, Axis Capital BUY ₹4,800 (from SELL ₹3,400 in May), DRChoksey ₹4,612 (rated negative on valuation) and Prabhudas Lilladher HOLD ₹4,498. Older standing calls: Elara BUY ₹4,698 (May), AMSEC BUY ₹3,817 (Mar) and JM Financial REDUCE ₹3,505 (Feb). Simply Wall St counted 15 analysts with an average target of ₹4,624 after Q1, only ~5% above the 30-Sep price. Bulls point to fluoropolymer share gains, R32 and the battery ramp; bears to valuation and battery delays.

blocks.h: How the street values Gujarat Fluorochemicals

blocks.p: Most brokers that disclose a method put **one multiple on FY28E consolidated earnings**: Prabhudas Lilladher 52x P/E; ICICI Direct 30x EV/EBITDA, which is ~54x P/E. Neither values the battery business separately any more (ICICI Direct did in May). JM Financial (Feb) uses a sum of the parts with the battery business at ₹1,241 a share; Elara uses a DCF. We follow the majority: P/E, applied to the earnings the market will look at in September 2027 (Sep-28E: half FY28E, half FY29E).

blocks.callout: **What the cross-checks tell us.** EV/EBITDA (20x Sep-28E EBITDA less net debt at Sep-27E) gives ₹3,699, above the P/E target, because its 20x starts from GFL's five-year trailing EV/EBITDA median, which still includes the FY24-26 trough years. The DCF (₹1,513) is far lower: free cash flow is negative until the early 2030s because capex runs at ₹1,500-3,150 cr a year and working capital (held at the FY26 ratio, 65% of revenue including capital advances) grows with sales. Even at 41% (Q1FY27's 149 days) the DCF would be only ~₹2,557. Today's price needs the battery business to reach something close to management's ₹12,000 cr revenue potential.

sections.title: Our honest summary: buy the business, not at this price

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's leading fluoropolymer maker, integrated from fluorspar, gaining share as 3M and AGC leave; a refrigerant business enjoying an R32 windfall until India's 2028 freeze; and a ₹6,000 cr battery-materials build-out that could be large but has not yet shown revenue.

**What you are paying:** 49.6x our FY28E EPS and 44.9x Sep-28E, for a company earning ~8% on equity with net debt heading to ~₹7,029 cr. On the street's own method and our inputs the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). The EV/EBITDA cross-check is higher (its starting multiple is not cleaned of trough years); the DCF is far lower.

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: A plastic or rubber made with fluorine (PTFE, PFA, FEP, PVDF, FKM); resists heat, chemicals and fire.
Polytetrafluoroethylene (best known as Teflon) and two melt-processable relatives used in cables, tubing and semiconductor parts.
Polyvinylidene fluoride: used in coatings, chemical plants and as the binder in lithium-ion battery electrodes.
Fluoroelastomer: a heat- and fuel-resistant rubber used in seals for cars and chemical plants.
Refrigerant gases; R22 is an HCFC being phased out, the others are HFCs used in air-conditioners, fridges and car ACs.
The global agreement to cut HFC production; India freezes output from 2028 at a 2024-26 baseline.
"Forever chemicals": thousands of fluorinated substances; the EU is preparing a broad restriction.
Battery materials: the lithium salt, the liquid that carries it, the cathode powder (lithium iron phosphate) and the graphite electrode.
Compulsorily convertible preference shares: here IFC's ₹430 cr in GFCL EV, which will turn into its equity.
Anhydrous hydrofluoric acid (basic fluorine raw material) and tetrafluoroethylene (the building block of PTFE).
